articles.title: 18 Best Bar Soaps, Tested by Editors | NBC Select 2026
articles.summary: Bar soaps work as effectively as body washes and I rounded up editor-approved picks from Dove, L’Occitane, Avène and more.
articles.body: For years I avoided bar soaps because I only associated them with my skin feeling tight and dry, something I wanted to avoid at any cost. Instead, I relied on liquid body washes or shower oils. While reporting and testing bar soaps for this story, I noticed a shift in many of their formulas — they’re not as drying as I always thought and work as well as a traditional body wash. (That dryness typically came from formulas with unbalanced pH levels — something many brands have now adjusted for, according to Dr. William Huang, a board-certified dermatologist and adjunct professor at Duke University.) To help debunk common bar soap misconceptions, I spoke to three board-certified dermatologists about their advantages over body washes and what to consider when shopping for one. Alongside the help of my colleagues, I also tested some popular options. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Best bar soaps of 2026 Below, I compiled expert-recommended bar soaps, ones our team tried and liked, as well as highly rated options from popular drugstore brands like Cerave and Panoxyl. Best non-exfoliating bar soaps Best overall In general, most dermatologists will recommend a bar of Dove Sensitive Skin Soap, says Dr. Maya K. Thosani, a board-certified dermatologist at Modern Dermatology in Scottsdale, Arizona. That’s because it effectively cleanses the skin without irritating it, she says. Along with cleansing agents, it also has some of Dove’s moisturizing cream to combat dryness and help the skin retain moisture, according to the brand. Dove’s bar soaps are also a favorite of NBC Selected staff. “It’s a drugstore classic for a reason,” says NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown. “Just a good old fashioned soap for people who don’t want to fuss with a long or expensive skin care routine.” Editor’s pick NBC Selected updates editor Mili Godio, who has dry and sensitive skin, says this bar soap keeps her skin “perfectly soft and hydrated”. Each bar is infused with olive and argan oils to keep skin moisturised, and are fully plant-based and hypoallergenic, according to the brand. “This bar soap not only smells amazing —I have it in multiple scents, but chamomile lavender is my favorite— but it’s also huge, so it lasts for several weeks,” says Godio. Best for sensitive skin This NBC Selected staff-favorite bar soap, which you can use on both your face and body, helps preserve moisture in your skin, according to the brand. “The lather is milky and hydrating, and it makes my skin feel nourished,” says former NBC Selected editorial projects manager Rebecca Rodriguez, who has sensitive skin. You can use it morning and night, and because it’s unscented, it’s great for those with sensitive skin. It also has ingredients to help soothe skin and reduce irritation and itchiness. Best for eczema After his dermatologist recommended this years ago, NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez uses this gentle, non-irritating bar on his face and body. “It does a great job keeping my skin moisturized hours after a shower,” he says. The soap, which has the National Eczema Association’s Seal of Acceptance, is also free of common irritants like fragrances, according to the brand. Best for dry skin This bar soap is great for those with especially dry skin since it has ceramides and hyaluronic acid, two popular ingredients that are key for hydrated skin. It’s also soap-free, meaning it cleanses the skin without compromising moisture or disrupting your skin barrier, according to experts in our guide to the best body washes for sensitive skin. Reviewers say it creates a rich and creamy lather and doesn’t cause any unwanted breakouts or flare-ups. It’s one of the most affordable options on this list and has a 4.7-star average rating from over 5,600 reviews on Amazon. Best unscented Ayeya is one of our favorite Black-owned beauty brands, and this natural African black soap from the brand is a favorite of NBC Selected updates editor Mili Godio. “Since I combine my bar soap with a hydrating body wash, I want something that’s gentle and not too fragranced,” she says. “This Ayeya bar is one of my favorites — a little goes a very long way, and it leaves my skin feeling soft and hydrated. Best of all, it never irritates my dry, sensitive skin.” It’s so gentle that you can even use it on your face and as a shaving lather, according to the brand. Best for face and body “I understand that from the outside looking in, someone covering their face in beef tallow seems gross, but my skin has never looked or felt better,” says Brown. “I discovered this brand on a solo road trip and, out of curiosity, decided to give this a shot. My hormonal breakouts have decreased and I’m not even close to finishing the bar I bought well over six months ago — it lasts a very long time.” Most gentle Fernandez also loves using this Cetaphil bar because it’s extremely gentle and “by far the most moisturizing one I’ve ever tried,” he says. The soap-free formula has ingredients that prevent the skin from drying out, and protect it from irritation, including tightness, according to the brand. Plus, you can use it on your face and body. Best budget pick “I loved everything about this lemon verbena-scented soap,” says Fernandez, who received a sample from the brand. “It’s the perfect size for holding in your hand, and the 12 rounded knobs on it make it easy to hold on to.” You can also use the knobs as a tension reliever over your muscles while you cleanse your skin, according to the brand. Most creamy lather When I want a bar soap that’s gentle and non-irritating on my dry, sensitive skin, I typically reach for this option from L’Occitane. It leaves my skin feeling moisturized, and though I generally avoid products with added or artificial fragrances, this one’s scented very subtly, so it doesn’t trigger or worsen my eczema patches. Its creamy lather is also great for shaving because it creates a slippery surface that makes it easy to swipe my razor over. Strongest scent This bar soap removes sweat, dirt and oil using mango butter, avocado oil and niacinamide. “This is one of those soaps that smacks you in the face with a distinct scent, which isn’t bad at all, but I think if you’re searching for a more subtle scent, this might not be your best option,” says former NBC Selected commerce editor Jordan Bowman, who received the sandalwood scent from the brand. Best for active lifestyles This plant-based soap uses ingredients like glycerin and a blend of oils (including tea tree and eucalyptus oil) to cleanse the skin and prevent fungal conditions, according to the brand. The oils help reduce the overgrowth of bacteria that’s caused by consistent sweaty conditions from working out and using communal gym equipment, according to Solpri. The soap has a 4.5-star average rating from more than 3,800 reviews on Amazon. Best exfoliating bar soaps Best for acne-prone skin This bar soap, which has a 4.6-star average rating from over 3,100 reviews on Amazon, uses benzoyl peroxide to treat and prevent breakouts. Reviewers say it helps control their acne, including whiteheads and blackheads, on their chest, back and face without leaving their skin feeling too dry and tight. “I use the liquid version of this whenever I have some breakouts bubbling up and I love how quickly it dries pimples up,” says former NBC Selected senior editor Lindsay Schneider. “The formula’s definitely on the stronger side so I don’t use it every day.” Best for uneven skin texture NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin enjoys using this watermelon-scented exfoliating bar, which has a light aroma, since it’s not too intense on her skin. “There are little poppy seeds in the bar, which act as an exfoliant, but they’re quite gentle and don’t irritate my sensitive skin,” says Malin, who received a courtesy sample from the brand. The poppy seeds throughout the bar help smooth out dry and bumpy skin for an overall smoother and even texture, according to Jukebox. “The bar also fits perfectly in the palm of my hand, so it’s very easy to get a good grip on.” Best exfoliating option “This produces a milky lather with very little effort and is gentle on my sensitive skin, leaving me feeling soft and moisturized.” The brand’s bar soaps come in a fragrance-free version as well as multiple fragrance options, too. “The scent is soothing without feeling overwhelming,” says Rodriguez. “I also like that the scent lingers on me more than other soaps or body washes I have used.” Each bar is formulated with goat milk, which has alpha-hydroxy acids (a chemical exfoliant) in it to remove dead skin, along with vitamin A to reduce fine lines, acne and more, according to the brand. Best scrub After receiving a sample from the brand, Malin loves using this coffee-scented bar soap to wake herself up in the morning because it makes her skin and bathroom smell like a cup of espresso. “The soap develops a creamy, sudsy lather as I use it, and I found it to be very moisturizing, and my skin feels softer afterward,” she says. “There are exfoliating coffee grounds in the bar, and they’re very gentle on my sensitive skin, which I appreciate. It’s technically designed for men, though anyone can really use it, according to Malin. Best splurge “I’ve noticed that bar soap sometimes makes my skin feel really dry, but my skin felt hydrated and clean after using this,” says NBC Selected social media assistant Caitlin Cusack, who received a sample from the brand. “The scrub was gentle on my skin but still left it feeling soft and smooth.” She also loves that its larger size makes it easier to grip and less likely to slip out of her hands. How I picked the best bar soap To help make this list and determine which bar soaps our team wanted to test, I spoke with experts about what to keep in mind: Skin type: This plays a significant role in determining which bar soap is best for you. If you have dry skin, you’ll want formulas with moisturizing ingredients, including glycerin and shea butter. If you have sensitive skin, you should avoid triggers like physical exfoliants and fragrances. For those with oily and acne-prone skin, consider options with chemical exfoliants that will combat breakouts and excess oil. Our list has options for all skin types.Function: Although the primary function of a bar soap is to cleanse the skin, many options on the market double as an exfoliating treatment. We have both non-exfoliating bar soaps and exfoliating ones on our list.Price: Bar soap tends to be budget-friendly — much more so than shower oils or liquid body washes. There are soaps as low as $4 on this list, with some even including value pack items where you can get multiple bars for under $20. How to shop for bar soaps Skin type and ingredients Your skin type is the most important factor to consider when shopping and regardless of your skin type, you should look for a hydrating formula. Hydrating ingredients typically come in the form of humectants, emollients and occlusives. Humectants, like glycerin, attract moisture to the skin, while emollients (like squalane/squalene) lock in moisture, and soothe and soften it, according to experts. Occlusives, like petrolatum, create a defensive layer that stops irritants from entering (ingredients like petrolatum) and also prevent water loss. Here’s what to look for beyond hydrating ingredients: If you have dry skin: The more moisturizing, the better. Look for formulas with shea butter, glycerin or other oils, according to Thosani.If you have oily skin: Exfoliating cleansers with either beta- or alpha-hydroxy acids will be best, says Thosani. They work by removing dead skin and debris to unclog pores and remove excess oil, according to experts in our guide to exfoliating.If you have sensitive skin: Look for fragrance-free options (not just unscented, which often has masking fragrances to make it smell neutral). You’ll do better with simple bar soap without parabens, essential oils and preservatives, according to Thosani.If you have acne-prone skin: Focus on antibacterial bar soaps (they typically come labeled as so) to help minimize breakouts. Proceed cautiously with them, however, because they can cause dryness and irritation, according to board-certified dermatologist Dr. Kseniya Kobets.If you have normal skin: You can really use anything and choose what formula you like based on your personal preferences, says Thosani. As important as it is to know what to look for, it’s equally important to know what to avoid. Huang recommends staying away from sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS), fragrances and parabens, as they can worsen eczema, dry skin and contact dermatitis. No matter your skin type, try to minimize the use of any gritty grains and grounds (like ground apricot or walnut pits) since they can be too abrasive and potentially damage the skin barrier, according to Thosani. Meet our dermatology experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. William Huang is a board-certified dermatologist and adjunct professor at Duke University’s School of Medicine.Dr. Kseniya Kobets is a board-certified dermatologist and director of cosmetic dermatology at Montefiore Einstein Advanced Care.Dr. Maya K. Thosani is a double board certified in dermatology and micrographic dermatologic surgery at Modern Dermatology in Scottsdale, Arizona. Why trust NBC Selected? Bianca Alvarez is a former associate reporter covering beauty and wellness, and has written extensively about body care, including stories on the best body lotions and body serums. For this story, she interviewed three board-certified dermatologists and shared their recommendations, as well as NBC Select-staff favorites that met their guidance. articles.title: Três são presos por sequestrar parente de ganhador da Mega-Sena no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: Em março, vítima de 16 anos foi sequestrada no Espírito Santo e mantida refém por dois dias em um cativeiro na Bahia. Prisões aconteceram seis meses após o crime.
articles.summary: Em março, vítima de 16 anos foi sequestrada no Espírito Santo e mantida refém por dois dias em um cativeiro na Bahia. Prisões aconteceram seis meses após o crime.
articles.body:
Operação Sorte Reversa prendeu três por sequestrar adolescente parente de ganhador da Mega-Sena no ES — Foto: Divulgação/Sesp

Três pessoas foram presas por sequestrarem a neta de um ganhador de R$ 99,5 milhões da Mega-Sena , uma adolescente de 16 anos, no Espírito Santo. As prisões aconteceram entre a sexta-feira (11) e este domingo (13).

O caso aconteceu há seis meses, em 16 de março deste ano, na cidade de Barra de São Francisco , no Noroeste capixaba. A menor foi encontrada dois dias depois em um cativeiro localizado em Nova Viçosa , na Bahia.

A Operação Sorte Reversa prendeu duas mulheres, ambas de 29 anos, na cidade de Teixeira de Freitas (BA). Uma das suspeitas foi encontrada na sexta-feira (11) e a outra neste domingo (13). O terceiro envolvido, um homem que não teve idade divulgada, foi localizado no sábado (12) em Linhares (ES).

A ação teve apoio das polícias Militar e Civil da Bahia, Polícia Penal do Espírito Santo e Notaer. Segundo a polícia, uma das mulheres teria alugado o carro usado no crime e a outra participado do sequestro.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, as identidades dos presos não foram divulgadas.

O delegado Leonardo Forattini detalhou a dinâmica do crime. Ele explicou que, na data, os suspeitos saíram da Bahia e passaram pela casa da moça com o veículo alugado.

Um deles fingiu estar passando mal e pediu um copo de água à moradora. Quando ela retornou de dentro da casa, dois homens desceram do veículo, pegaram a adolescente e fugiram. Ela foi levada para o cativeiro, onde permaneceu por dois dias.

Já a delegada Jéssica Bohrer, responsável pela delegacia de Barra de São Francisco, detalhou como ocorreram as negociações. Após o sequestro, a mãe da vítima começou a receber mensagens ameaçadoras pelo WhatsApp, enviadas por um suspeito que estava no presídio de Teixeira de Freitas.

"Eu assumi o perfil da mãe da adolescente e me passei por ela para negociar com o sequestrador na tentativa de ganhar tempo, identificar o suspeito e localizar onde a vítima estava mantida refém", explicou.

Em março deste ano, uma adolescente de 16 anos foi sequestrada em Barra de São Francisco, Noroeste do Espírito Santo, e mantida refém por dois dias em um cativeiro no distrito de Posto da Mata, cidade de Nova Viçosa, no estado da Bahia.

Segundo as investigações da Polícia Civil, que resultaram no resgate da jovem, o crime foi planejado após os criminosos descobrirem que um parente da vítima teria faturado um prêmio milionário da Mega-Sena no ano passado.

A ordem para a realização do crime teria partido de um detento do presídio de Teixeira de Freitas (BA), integrante da facção criminosa Comando Vermelho.

A intenção era sequestrar outra pessoa da família do vencedor do sorteio, explicou a adjunta da Delegacia Regional de Barra de São Francisco, delegada Jéssica Bohrer.

No entanto, os criminosos que realizaram a ação teriam tido dificuldades para executar o plano inicial de sequestrar uma neta consanguínea do premiado e acabaram capturando a adolescente que, apesar do parentesco, não tem vínculo consanguíneo com o ganhador do prêmio .

Após a confirmação do local onde a jovem era mantida refém, que se deu com o apoio da Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária da Bahia, policiais civis do Espírito Santo foram até Nova Viçosa e, em ação conjunta com forças de segurança locais, realizaram o cerco tático e a intervenção no imóvel.

A adolescente resgatada foi encaminhada ao estado capixaba e entregue à família. O valor do prêmio que o parente da adolescente teria faturado na Mega é de R$ 99,5 milhões.

Durante a operação, um dos criminosos, que portava um revólver calibre .32, resistiu e acabou sendo atingido durante confronto. Ele foi socorrido, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos e acabou morto. O suspeito foi identificado como Mauro Henrique Rodrigues de Oliveira, de 24 anos.

No local, também foram apreendidos uma arma de fogo, um veículo com restrição de roubo e aproximadamente 800 gramas de entorpecentes, como crack e maconha.

articles.title: Fervedor inderramável: como o bico evita a fervura escapando | G1
articles.standfirst: O nome descreve a função. Entenda como o desenho do fervedor contém a fervura que sobe e por que ele resolve leite, mingau e canjica
articles.summary: O nome descreve a função. Entenda como o desenho do fervedor contém a fervura que sobe e por que ele resolve leite, mingau e canjica
articles.body:
Leite, mingau, canjica e mungunzá têm algo em comum: sobem de repente e escapam da panela. O fervedor inderramável é um utensílio desenhado especificamente contra isso — e a solução não é mágica, é geometria: altura livre e um bico que direciona o que sobe de volta para dentro.

Fervedores inderramáveis em alumínio fundido craqueado, de 2 e 5 litros — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Leite forma película de proteína; mingau e canjica liberam amido , que cria espuma. Nos dois casos, o vapor fica preso sob essa camada e acumula pressão até romper — empurrando o conteúdo para cima de uma vez. Panela cheia e de parede baixa não tem para onde acomodar esse volume.

O amido cria espuma que aprisiona o vapor. Quando rompe, empurra tudo para cima de uma vez.

•Parede alta: deixa volume livre acima do conteúdo, absorvendo a subida.

•Bico de despejo: d ireciona o transbordo para dentro em vez de pela lateral.

•Fundo grosso de alumínio fundido: d istribui o calor e evita o ponto quente que forma espuma localizada.

•Cabo lateral: p ermite tirar do fogo rápido, que é a manobra que salva o preparo.

1. Não passe de d ois terços da altura, mesmo no fervedor.

2. Fogo m édio: fogo alto acelera a formação de espuma.

3.M exa periodicamente para romper a película antes de ela prender vapor.

4. Tenha o cabo livre e a mão por perto nos minutos finais.

O acabamento craqueado é o mais comum nessa peça, por esconder marcas de uso. Os fervedores inderramáveis vêm em 2 e 5 litros.

Modelos de 2 e 5 litros: parede alta e bico que contêm a subida — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com panelas e fervedores em alumínio fundido. Os modelos estão no catálogo de fervedores , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: Homem é resgatado com vida após cair e ser levado pela correnteza no Rio Atibaia, em Campinas; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 46 anos foi levada por cerca de 500 metros na água, ficou agarrada à vegetação e foi retirada após uma operação de resgate com auxílio de canoísta em Sousas, na noite de sábado (12).
articles.summary: Vítima de 46 anos foi levada por cerca de 500 metros na água, ficou agarrada à vegetação e foi retirada após uma operação de resgate com auxílio de canoísta em Sousas.
articles.body:
Um homem de 46 anos foi resgatado com vida após cair e ser arrastado pela correnteza do Rio Atibaia, no distrito de Sousas, em Campinas (SP), na noite de sábado (12). Um morador ouviu pedidos de socorro e acionou canoístas para auxiliar nas buscas até a chegada do resgate - assista acima .

"Meu Deus, que susto. Deus abençoe. Graças a Deus cara, você me salvou", disse a vítima ao canoísta Pedro Coelho assim que foi retirada da água.

Quando foi localizado, José Luiz estava agarrado à vegetação na margem oposta do rio. Coelho foi o primeiro chegar até o homem, e disse que ele já estava bastante debilitado quando foi encontrado.

"Tinha bebido água do rio, tinha se afogado bastante, nadou um bom trecho, pelo menos uns 500 metros. Eu peguei ele e coloquei em cima do caiaque porque ele não sabia até quando ia conseguir ficar se segurando ali", disse.

Segundo Pedro Coelho, foram cerca de duas horas com a vítima em cima do caiaque até que o trabalho do resgate fosse concluído, pela dificuldade da operação.

"O tempo todo eu fui conversando com ele, porque ele apresentava pequenos sinais de delírio de vez em quando. Ele não conseguia ficar sentado. Ele pendia o corpo para o lado, estava extremamente cansado".

Homem de 46 anos foi resgatado com vida após cair e ser arrastado pela correnteza do rio Atibaia, no distrito de Sousas, em Campinas (SP); canoísta Pedro Coelho participou do resgate — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, a vítima havia ingerido água, apresentava sinais de hipotermia e tinha um ferimento em um dos olhos .

Entre a chamada da corporação ao fim da operação, foram 2h22.

A vítima foi levada até uma área com acesso por terra, onde recebeu atendimento das equipes de emergência e foi encaminhada ao Pronto-Socorro Anchieta.

O g1 tenta confirmar o estado de saúde do homem com a prefeitura de Campinas.

articles.title: Guyana’s oil boom and challenges
articles.summary: Guyana’s president says his country has seen an increase in oil revenue as the Iran conflict reshapes global markets.
articles.body:
President Mohamed Irfaan Ali insists he does not want Guyana to depend solely on its oil wealth.

In recent months, oil revenues in the South American country have increased sharply as the US-Israel war on Iran grinds on, disrupting global energy supplies and driving up the price of crude oil.

In conversation with Talk to Al Jazeera, Ali says that major oil discoveries 11 years ago have transformed the country.

Despite the oil boom, inflation and the cost of living remain high. The opposition says the government is mishandling the oil wealth, but the president rejects those accusations.

Ali says that his government is striving to diversify other sectors of the economy to ensure long-term growth.

In this discussion, Guyana’s president says he’s not worried about United States intervention in neighbouring Venezuela, noting that the administration of US President Donald Trump is helping coordinate security in the region.

articles.title: Estupro de vulnerável em Volta Redonda: foragido é preso pela DEAM | G1
articles.standfirst: Prisão aconteceu no bairro Água Limpa. Segundo a Delegacia Especializada de Atendimento à Mulher (DEAM), ele é suspeito de violentar a enteada, de 13 anos.
articles.summary: A DEAM prendeu no bairro Água Limpa um homem de 40 anos suspeito de estupro de vulnerável contra a enteada de 13 anos em Volta Redonda.
articles.body:
Deam de Volta Redonda,RJ — Foto: Jeniffer Marcato/TV Rio Sul

Um homem, de 40 anos, que estava foragido da Justiça por estupro de vulnerável, foi preso no sábado (12) em Volta Redonda (RJ). O caso aconteceu no bairro Água Limpa.

Segundo a Delegacia Especializada de Atendimento à Mulher (Deam), o suspeito, que estava foragido da Justiça há mais de 60 dias, foi encontrado após um monitoramento contínuo, que possibilitou o mapeamento do paradeiro dele.

Ainda de acordo com a Deam, ele é suspeito de violentar a própria enteada, de 13 anos. Contra ele, havia um mandado de prisão em aberto por estupro de vulnerável.

A Delegacia Especializada de Atendimento à Mulher informou ainda que ele foi encontrado e preso em um imóvel no bairro Água Limpa.

O homem foi encaminhado para a DEAM, onde o caso foi registrado. Em seguida, ele foi transferido para o sistema prisional, onde está à disposição da Justiça.

A identidade do envolvido não foi divulgada.

articles.title: Círios reúnem milhares de fiéis em Tomé-Açu, Terra Alta e Cachoeira do Arari, no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Tomé-Açu, cerca de 10 mil pessoas acompanharam o Círio de Santa Maria. Procissões também foram realizadas em Terra Alta e Cachoeira do Arari.
articles.summary: Em Tomé-Açu, cerca de 10 mil pessoas acompanharam o Círio de Santa Maria. Procissões também foram realizadas em Terra Alta e Cachoeira do Arari.
articles.body:
Três Círios realizados neste domingo (13) reuniram milhares de fiéis em Tomé-Açu, Terra Alta e Cachoeira do Arari , no Pará. Em Tomé-Açu, cerca de 10 mil pessoas participaram do Círio de Santa Maria. Em Terra Alta, centenas acompanharam a procissão de Nossa Senhora do Livramento, enquanto cerca de 1,5 mil pessoas participaram do Círio de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, em Cachoeira do Arari, no Marajó.

A 65ª edição do Círio de Santa Maria percorreu cerca de quatro quilômetros pelas ruas de Tomé-Açu. A procissão saiu da Comunidade Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, no bairro da Campina, conduzindo a imagem da padroeira.

Segundo a organização, aproximadamente 10 mil pessoas acompanharam o cortejo. A edição deste ano teve como tema “Com Santa Maria, Mãe da Igreja, somos discípulos e discípulas missionários”.

O manto da imagem foi confeccionado em tons de rosa e produzido e doado pela família Oliveira.

Reconhecido como Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial do município, o Círio abriu a programação da festividade de Santa Maria, que segue até 20 de setembro com atividades religiosas e culturais.

Círio Nossa Senhora do Livramento — Foto: Ascom

Em Terra Alta, centenas de fiéis se concentraram em frente à antiga Igreja Matriz na manhã deste domingo para uma missa presidida pelo padre Roberto Mesquita. Após a celebração, a imagem de Nossa Senhora do Livramento seguiu em procissão pelas ruas da cidade.

A programação começou na sexta-feira (11), com uma procissão rodoviária. No sábado (12), foram realizados o 4º Círio Fluvial e a primeira Romaria Equestre. Durante o Círio Fluvial, a imagem foi conduzida pelo Rio Marapanim.

A berlinda deste domingo foi ornamentada com flores em tons de amarelo, salmão, branco e verde. A festividade tem como tema “Com a Virgem do Livramento, prepararemos o caminho do Senhor” e segue até o próximo domingo (20).

Em Cachoeira do Arari, na Ilha do Marajó, cerca de 1,5 mil pessoas participaram do 58º Círio de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, realizado pela Igreja Matriz de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, na Vila de Retiro Grande.

Círio de Cachoeira do Arari, no Marajó — Foto: Ascom

A procissão saiu da Comunidade de Santa Rita de Cássia, em Jacaretuba, e percorreu aproximadamente quatro quilômetros pelos ramais da região. O tema desta edição foi “Virgem de Nazaré, cubra-nos com teu manto de amor”.

O Círio também marcou os três anos de fundação da comunidade como paróquia.

Neste ano, a imagem de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré usou um manto azul pintado à mão e com aplicações de rosas. A peça foi confeccionada por Marcos Ferreira, natural de Retiro Grande e morador de Belém , que, segundo a organização, doa o manto há mais de 20 anos.

A celebração deste domingo encerrou a festividade e foi presidida pelo administrador diocesano, padre Antônio Cardoso. Após a missa, a programação teve atividades culturais e o tradicional bingo do Círio.

articles.summary: Confira as atividades de campanha de Araceli Lemos; Daniel Santos; Gal Leite; Hana Ghassan; Ruth Reis e Well Macêdo.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao Governo do Pará nas Eleições 2026 — Foto: Reprodução

Os candidatos ao governo do Pará cumpriram compromissos de campanha neste sábado (12) e domingo (13).

Entre as atividades do fim de semana, os candidatos realizaram caminhadas, reuniões com apoiadores, carreatas, comício, inauguração de comitês eleitorais, rodas de conversa e panfletagem.

Os eventos foram realizados em Belém e também em cidades do interior do estado.

O primeiro turno das eleições está marcado para o dia 4 de outubro de 2026. O segundo turno, caso seja necessário, ocorrerá no dia 25 do mesmo mês.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato, em ordem alfabética:

No sábado (12), a candidata iniciou a manhã com uma caminhada no Complexo do Ver-o-Peso, em Belém, seguida de uma reunião plenária com apoiadores de sua candidatura. Araceli também participou da inauguração do comitê de campanha de candidatos a deputado federal e estadual.

No domingo (13) pela manhã, a candidata participou de uma caminhada em apoio à candidatura presidencial de sua coligação, com concentração na Escadinha do Cais do Porto, em Belém.

Pela manhã, o candidato Daniel Santos cumpriu agenda no município de Barcarena , onde realizou mobilização com concentração na Praia do Caripi. À tarde, o candidato seguiu para Abaetetuba , cumprindo agenda de campanha com concentração na Rua Frei José de Manaus.

No domingo (13), o candidato realizou uma caminhada pela manhã no distrito de Icoaraci, em Belém, com concentração no cruzamento da Rua Siqueira Mendes com a Travessa São Roque.

Até a publicação desta matéria, a assessoria da candidata não enviou a agenda de compromissos realizados no fim de semana.

No sábado (12), a candidata Hana Ghassan cumpriu, pela manhã, compromissos de governo em Paragominas . Em seguida, ela realizou agenda de campanha com reuniões no município. No fim da tarde, realizou uma caminhada no bairro Jaderlândia, também em Paragominas.

No domingo (13) pela manhã, a candidata Hana Ghassan realizou uma carreata no bairro da pratinha, na capital paraense.

No sábado (12), a candidata Ruth Reis dedicou o período da manhã a atividades administrativas de campanha. À tarde, esteve no Instituto Teológico Quadrangular (ITQ) e, à noite, participou de um culto, seguido de panfletagem.

No domingo (13), a candidata participou de programações religiosas no bairro da Marambaia, em Belém, nos períodos da manhã e da noite. À tarde, a candidata realizou reuniões de organização e planejamento para entrevista na TV liberal.

No sábado (12), a candidata iniciou o dia acompanhando um evento de trabalhadores da educação, em Belém. Em seguida, visitou uma feira de empreendedorismo feminino. À tarde, participou de uma roda de conversa sobre mulheres trabalhadoras e eleições, no bairro do Mangueirão.

No domingo (13) pela manhã, a candidata realizou caminhada e panfletagem no distrito de Mosqueiro, em Belém

articles.title: Doação de órgãos: marido em Araxá autoriza gesto após morte da esposa | G1
articles.standfirst: Lílian Raquel Duarte da Silva morreu aos 49 anos após sofrer um AVC hemorrágico e teve as córneas e os rins doados. Segundo o marido, a decisão foi inspirada pela vontade que ela sempre teve de ajudar.
articles.summary: No Setembro Verde, Adriano Duarte da Silva autorizou a doação de órgãos da esposa Lílian, que faleceu após um AVC, honrando sua vontade de sempre ajudar.
articles.body:
Lílian Raquel Duarte da Silva morreu aos 49 anos — Foto: Adriano Duarte / Divulgação

Depois de 31 anos ao lado da esposa, o técnico de projetos Adriano Duarte da Silva, de 53 anos, precisou tomar uma decisão difícil: autorizar a doação dos órgãos dela. Lílian Raquel Duarte da Silva tinha 49 anos quando faleceu, vítima de um AVC hemorrágico, em janeiro de 2024, em Araxá .

Com a autorização de Adriano, as córneas e os rins dela foram doados. Segundo ele, nunca havia conversado com a mulher sobre o assunto, mas decidiu permitir a doação porque sabia o quanto ela gostava de ajudar outras pessoas.

Adriano lembra que o problema de saúde da esposa começou em 11 de dezembro de 2024 quando Lílian estava na igreja, onde dava aulas de crisma e passou mal.

“Ela sentiu uma forte dor de cabeça e perdeu os movimentos do corpo. Eu, imediatamente levei ela para o hospital, mas o problema não foi identificado naquele momento. Nos dias seguintes, ela continuou apresentando mal-estar”, contou.

Na noite de 1º de janeiro, Lílian foi para o quarto mais cedo. Pouco depois, acabou caindo no chão.

Adriano prestou os primeiros socorros e ela foi levada novamente para o hospital. Desta vez, não voltou para casa.

Ela permaneceu internada por quatro dias em coma até falecer. A causa da morte foi um AVC hemorrágico.

Depois que os médicos informaram à família que não havia mais possibilidade de recuperação em decorrência da falência cerebral, uma equipe conversou com Adriano e os filhos sobre a possibilidade de doação. A decisão foi tomada naquele momento.

Lílian e Adriano nunca haviam conversado sobre o assunto. Ainda assim, ele diz que a escolha fazia sentido diante da forma como ela vivia.

“Ela sempre ajudava na igreja. Era algo da personalidade dela ajudar ao próximo”, afirmou.

Foram autorizadas as doações das córneas e dos rins. O coração também chegou a ser avaliado para transplante, mas não pôde ser aproveitado porque foram constatados rompimentos de vasos.

Adriano não sabe quem recebeu os órgãos e diz que gostaria de conhecer as pessoas que foram beneficiadas. “Queria conhecer para quem foi doado, ficaria feliz”, contou.

Lílian era empresária e mãe de três filhos. A morte dela foi devastadora para a família, que mesmo em meio à dor, não teve dúvidas ao tomar a decisão de autorizar a doação dos órgãos.

“Mesmo com o luto e a dor do momento, tendo a possibilidade de ajudar, sempre é bom”, contou Adriano.

Aumentar o número de decisões como a da família da Lílian é um desafio no Brasil. Em 2025, o país bateu o recorde de transplantes de órgãos e tecidos, mas os dados do Registro Brasileiro de Transplantes, divulgados este mês, revelam que em cerca de 45% dos casos, parentes não autorizaram a doação dos órgãos após a constatação da morte de familiares.

Atitudes como a que foi tomada por Adriano após a morte da esposa ganham ainda mais significado no Setembro Verde, mês dedicado à conscientização e ao incentivo à doação de órgãos e tecidos no Brasil.

A campanha reforça a importância do Dia Nacional da Doação de Órgãos, celebrado em 27 de setembro. No caso da família de Araxá, a decisão foi tomada em meio ao luto e a uma espera dolorosa: foram dois dias entre a morte de Lílian e a captação dos órgãos, antes que a amigos e parentes pudessem finalmente realizar o velório e se despedir.

De acordo com o Ministério da Saúde, no primeiro semestre de 2026 foram realizados 17.458 transplantes de órgãos no Brasil. Nos últimos anos, graças à conscientização das famílias, o número de procedimentos vem aumentando.

Em 2022 foram 25.641 transplantes. Em 2023, foram 28.769 procedimentos; em 2024, foram 30.313 registros; e, em 2025, 30.986.

No Brasil, o SUS é quem realiza os transplantes de órgãos (coração, pulmão, fígado, rim, pâncreas, intestino e multivisceral), medula óssea, córnea, pele, tecidos musculoesqueléticos, válvulas cardíacas e membrana amniótica. O país adota o modelo de lista única de espera, gerido pelo Sistema Nacional de Transplantes (SNT), com priorização baseada em critérios técnicos e clínicos, além da compatibilidade entre doador e receptor.

Lilian e Adriano ficaram casados por 31 anos e tiveram 3 filhos — Foto: Adriano Duarte / Divulgaç

A legislação brasileira prevê que a retirada de órgãos, tecidos ou partes do corpo para transplante após a morte exige o consentimento formal de familiares. Ou seja, ainda que em vida a pessoa tenha demonstrado a vontade de autorizar a doação, após o falecimento, o procedimento só pode ser feito com a permissão dos familiares. Por isso, conversar abertamente com as pessoas próximas é fundamental para que a autorização seja concedida.

Adriano conheceu Lílian quando ela tinha 17 anos. Os dois permaneceram juntos por 31 anos e tiveram três filhos: dois adultos, de 26 e 22 anos, e um adolescente, de 13. Para a família, Lílian deixou a lembrança de uma mulher que gostava de cuidar de si, da família e das pessoas ao redor.

A religiosidade também fazia parte da rotina dela. Era na igreja que dava aulas de crisma e onde, segundo o marido, exercia uma das características que mais marcaram sua personalidade, que era a disposição para ajudar. Foi essa lembrança que também pesou na decisão de autorizar a doação.

Para Adriano, a possibilidade de ajudar outras pessoas não elimina a dor da perda, mas dá um novo significado a uma decisão tomada em meio ao luto. “Independente do luto e da dor do momento, tendo a possibilidade de ajudar, sempre é bom”.

articles.title: Guarujá abre 54 vagas para cursos de gastronomia e bijuterias | G1
articles.standfirst: Cursos são oferecidos pelo Fundo Social de Solidariedade de Guarujá (FSS), em parceria com o Sebrae-SP e o Senac. As inscrições seguem até as turmas serem preenchidas.
articles.summary: Cursos de capacitação em Guarujá são oferecidos pelo Fundo Social em parceria com Sebrae e Senac com foco em gastronomia e bijuterias.
articles.body:
Aprenda a fazer fotografia com celular para gastronomia é um dos cursos disponíveis em Guarujá — Foto: Centro Europeu

A Prefeitura de Guarujá, no litoral de São Paulo, abriu 54 vagas para cursos de capacitação profissional. A iniciativa acontece por meio de uma parceria entre o Fundo Social de Solidariedade de Guarujá (FSS), o Sebrae-SP e o Senac. As inscrições seguem até as turmas serem preenchidas.

De acordo com a prefeitura, há vagas para os cursos de fotografia para gastronomia, preparo e venda de bolos e tortas e criação, montagem e venda de bijuterias. São 18 inscritos por turma ( veja abaixo as datas e horários ).

As aulas acontecem no Centro de Atividades Educacionais e Comunitárias (Caec) Isabel Ortega situado à Rua Manoel da Cruz Michael nº 333, no Santa Rosa.

Para se matricular, os interessados devem comparecer ao local e apresentar os seguintes documentos: RG ou CNH (cópia), comprovante de residência (cópia) e duas fotos.

Confira as datas e os horários das aulas de cada curso abaixo:

Aprenda a fazer fotografia com celular para gastronomia Datas: 08, 09, 14, 15, 16 e 19/10 Horário: 13h às 17h

Prepare e venda bolos e tortas Datas: 14, 15, 16, 19 e 20/10 Horário: 13h às 17h

Aprenda a criar, montar e vender bijuterias Datas: 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, 18, 19 e 23/11 Horário: 13h às 17h

articles.title: Chester Zoo mistakenly advertises 'child predator tour' tickets
articles.summary: Chester Zoo, which was selling tickets to see lions and tigers, says the mistake was a computer error.
articles.body:
A zoo has blamed a computer error after it advertised a "child predator tour" online to see its tigers and lions.

Bosses at Chester Zoo quickly changed the 90-minute bus tour's name after it was branded "sinister" by visitors.

A zoo spokeswoman said the error was "due to our default naming convention in our system", but it was "quickly changed".

The name blunder earlier this week was part of the Cheshire zoo's ticket promotion to allow visitors to go on a tour showcasing its Sumatran tigers, lions, rhinos and Komodo dragons.

The mistake was mocked by the zoo's customers and visitors online.

One remarked: "I hope this has been cleared by Cheshire Police - seems a bit dangerous."

Another said: "Staggering - how did that get approved?"

The private bus tour cost £25 for children. 'Adult predator' tickets were also advertised by mistake for £30.

The zoo's website said: "Discover the predators of the animal kingdom, and their prey in our brand new guided tour.

"You'll be the first visitors in the zoo as you board our electric tour bus and enjoy 90 minutes of the zoo all to yourself.

"Come face to face with some of the zoo's most iconic animals, away from the crowds, including our family of Sumatran tigers.

"Your expert tour guides will be on hand to share fascinating facts about some of nature's most effective hunters."

articles.title: Atherstone baby death suspects released on police bail
articles.summary: The woman, 19, and man aged 21, were detained on Friday after the girl's death in Atherstone.
articles.body:
Two people arrested in connection with the death of a one-year-old girl in Warwickshire have been released on bail, police say.

It comes after emergency services were called to a house on Long Street, Atherstone, at about 11:50 BST on Friday to reports of a child in cardiac arrest. She was pronounced dead at the scene a short while later, police said.

A 19-year-old woman and a man aged 21 were then both arrested at the scene on suspicion of child neglect.

Later the pair were further arrested on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child, said Warwickshire Police.

Det Ch Insp Martyn Kendall said: "This tragic death has understandably caused a great deal of shock and concern in the local community.

"The two suspects arrested have now been bailed with strict conditions."

The force said officers were waiting for a post-mortem examination to be carried out to help shed more light on the circumstances leading up to her death.

Anyone with information has been urged to contact the force.

articles.title: New Welsh Senedd constituency names to be reviewed
articles.summary: A review of constituencies used in May's Welsh Senedd could see Welsh-only names changed.
articles.body:
New constituency names in Wales - used for the first time in this May's Senedd election - are going to be reviewed and possibly changed.

It means the 16 constituencies could see changes to Welsh-only names that proved unpopular, with any amendments set to be in place by the 2030 election.

Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru chief executive Shereen Williams said the review would ensure constituencies reflected the communities they serve, including cultural heritage and Welsh language use.

The 2025 review paired UK parliamentary constituencies - for MPs - and former Welsh Senedd areas to create 16 new constituencies for May's Senedd expansion, with six Members of the Senedd representing each.

This saw the number of MSs increase from 60 to 96, with 40 constituencies and five regions changed to 16 areas.

Williams told BBC Radio Wales' Sunday Supplement that the new Welsh-only consistency names could also be revised following public consultation as they did not prove popular with everyone .

She added that legislation required the use of single names where possible, but said: "If we are unable to find a name that reflects the identity of the area, or that's completely unrecognisable, it has nothing to do with the area, then we would then consider bilingual names.

"These set of boundaries that were used for the recent set of elections were always meant to be temporary. We're not we're not starting from a blank slate.

"Some people thought we would be wiping off all the boundaries and rebuilding them.

"No, we are going to start from the boundaries that were used in the recent Senedd elections and go from there."

She said the plan was to ensure equal population spread per constituency based on figures from the latest census - about 150,000 people in each, within a margin of 10%, so between 135,000-165,000.

Officials also want to align communities that share cultural similarities, before going out to a public consultation, expected in 2027.

The review is expected to be completed in time for the next elections in 2030.

A follow-up review is also planned in 2038, which could see further changes.

articles.title: National Memorial Arboretum dedicates memorial to veterans who died by suicide
articles.summary: Hundreds attend a dedication service at the National Memorial Arboretum for the Elysium Memorial.
articles.body:
Hundreds of people have gathered at the National Memorial Arboretum for the dedication of a permanent tribute to veterans and armed forces personnel who have died by suicide.

The Elysium Memorial , at the site in Alrewas, Staffordshire, is the first permanent memorial of its kind to be built in the UK.

More than 1,300 military veterans and personnel have taken their lives in the last 30 years, with the memorial aiming to provide a place for contemplation for those affected by the loss of a friend or loved one.

Edward Mackenzie, co-founder of the Elysium Memorial Foundation, which is behind the project, said he was "blown away" by the number of people that had turned up.

More than 300 motorcyclist rode to the arboretum from Burton-on-Trent on Sunday, with a convoy organised by community organisation Wheels for Wishes.

Mackenzie, who served in the army for more than 30 years and has lost over to 20 friends to suicide, including his best friend, said seeing those veterans' being recognised "means everything".

"This is why I did it, I did for for the friends, the families, the comrades, those that we've lost to suicide," he told the BBC.

"There's a lot of families here today that have been thanking me for achieving this memorial so I'm incredibly grateful."

There were 277 cases of veterans taking their own lives between 2006 and 2025, according to the Ministry of Defence.

"Any death by suicide is a tragedy that is felt across our community, and our thoughts are with those who have been impacted by the loss of a loved one," a spokesperson said.

"The welfare of our armed forces is at the heart of everything we do - more than £25m invested into Op Courage in the last year and our £50m Valour programme gives veterans in England access to specialist NHS mental health services and access to essential care, continuing our steadfast commitment to provide our forces and their families the wellbeing support they deserve."

Following the ceremony, people at the arboretum were invited to lay their own wreaths at the memorial.

Mackenzie said he was "very emotional" about the size of the turnout.

"I'm lost for words a lot of the time and I hope that this memorial will really help towards the mental health and families and basically taking the word suicide out of the shadows," he explained.

"I think that we still have amazing work to do to try and help everyone."

If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .

articles.title: Eveline Ashbaugh was found stabbed to death on her Ohio llama farm on May 5, 2007 | Dateline
articles.summary: Sixty-year-old Eveline Ashbaugh was found stabbed to death on her llama farm outside Delaware City, Ohio, on May 5, 2007. Investigators have identified several persons of interest.
articles.body: On the morning of May 5, 2007, a farmhand in Delaware County, Ohio, placed a call to 911 after he showed up to work and his boss, Eveline Ashbaugh, was nowhere to be found. Deputies with the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office were dispatched to Eveline’s farm to search for her. What they found was a crime scene: 60-year-old Eveline had been stabbed to death in her bedroom. So began an investigation that has spanned nearly 20 years. Detective Sergeant Joshua Clarke is the third detective to work Eveline’s case. “One of the biggest issues with this case in particular is that there’s no shortage of potential persons of interest,” he told Dateline. Eveline’s farm was in a rural area, a couple of miles north of Delaware City. And Eveline was no ordinary farmer. “She had about 30 to 40 llamas,” Clarke said. “There’s money to be made with llama fur that -- it can go for a high amount. And then she was also working on establishing bloodlines and breeding rights.” Divorced and not in a relationship at the time of her death, Eveline lived alone in the farmhouse. “She did have a circle of friends,” Clarke said, adding that those friends described her as “kinda brusque and eccentric.” The last known contact with Eveline was between 11 p.m. and midnight on May 4, when she spoke to a friend on the phone. According to Clarke, investigators believe she was killed a few hours later, between 2 and 4 a.m. on May 5. Due to the clutter in the house, investigators didn’t locate Eveline during the initial search. “When they scoured the house a second time, that’s when they discovered her,” Clarke said. Eveline was found kneeling at the edge of her bed. “There was some miscellaneous jewelry on her back,” Clarke said. “One of the dresser drawers, a cloth, and a laundry basket had been placed on her head.” Based on the crime scene, investigators believed Eveline may have been killed by someone with a personal vendetta against her. She had been stabbed multiple times in her upper body. “It certainly appears to be a crime of passion. There’s certainly overkill,” he said. Investigators noticed a ladder propped up against the outside wall of the house that reached Eveline’s second-floor bedroom window. The window was open, but there were no signs of forced entry. Based on the location of Eveline’s body and the blood-spatter analysis, investigators don’t believe anyone came in through the window. Clarke told Dateline that investigators at the time believed the placement of the ladder was staged. “It’s far more likely that someone had come in through her bedroom door, and that the door into the residence was either unlocked or someone was able to unlock it,” he said. Because of the clutter, investigators found it difficult to determine whether anything of value had been taken from the residence. Her purse was in her vehicle, and it appeared to have been dumped out, but investigators found several hundred dollars in cash inside. “It’s possible they just dumped it out really quick and didn’t notice it, or it’s possible it was staged,” Clarke said. “My theory is that the primary reason to go there was to kill her, and that anything else would have been a secondary reason.” Investigators believe Eveline knew her killer -- or killers. “We haven’t discounted the theory that it was really potentially multiple people involved,” Clarke said. “It was definitely someone that would have known the residence, would have known her, would have known her routine.” As investigators dug into Eveline’s life, they looked closely at both her personal relationships and her business dealings. “There was this perception, we think, by some of the people that worked for her that she maybe had money, but the truth was she was financially destitute,” Clarke said, adding that according to Eveline’s business partner, the llama operation never made a profit. Clarke says it seemed like the constant financial strain was getting to Eveline. “We were told by almost everybody that worked for her that she was not pleasant to work for,” Clarke said. “They would quit ‘cause they just couldn’t stand working for her, and that she’d owed them money and never -- and wouldn’t pay them.” Investigators ruled out Eveline’s former romantic partners, such as her ex-husband and her business partner, with whom she had once been romantically involved. But according to Clarke, they were able to identify a few individuals whose romantic overtures Eveline had rejected. “The way that she was killed,” Clarke said, “indicates to us that it was someone that was very angry at her, potentially, or at least partially, for some kind of romantic slight.” Clarke says investigators have identified at least 10 potential persons of interest. “At least 10 people that I can’t rule out for various reasons,” Clarke said. “The victim was not well-liked by a lot of people. She had employed several people that had criminal histories, and a lot of the people that we had talked to did not have kind things to say about her.” According to Clarke, even the farmhand who called to report Eveline missing is considered a person of interest. Investigators also administered polygraph tests and Computer Voice Stress Analysis exams to several people. “We did have one person of interest that did take that and did fail,” Clarke said. “We have, um, a couple other persons of interest that took it and passed, and then we have another person of interest that said they would take it and then canceled and has not agreed to take anything since.” Physical evidence collected in the case has so far done little to narrow the list of persons of interest. A bloody, partial footprint was recovered at the scene. “We checked several shoes of various persons of interest,” Clarke said. “But we never found the matching tread.” DNA collected at the scene has also not led to answers. “A lot of the persons of interest provided DNA samples that were run against other DNA that was collected. Nothing has matched thus far,” Clarke said. The murder weapon was never found. “We did test several knives that we recovered from different scenes that were potentially connected, but none of those yielded a match,” Clarke said. Eveline’s case remains active, and investigators are now reevaluating the evidence. “In this past year or so is when there’s been new kind of movement on this case, but we don’t have new information per se,” Clarke explained. “It’s just looking at the old information and seeing if we can get anything different this time.” Clarke plans to request that some of the evidence be retested. “Nothing has been tested since it was initially submitted,” he said. “There’s been a lot of advancements and maybe things that we couldn’t test very well back then; there might be a better shot now.” Related: Dateline first learned of Eveline’s case when reporting on the 2001 cold case murder of Regina Hicks in Willard, Ohio. Former Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost told Dateline about his cold case initiative, which was created to help solve cases like Regina’s and Eveline’s. “We believe somebody out there knows, you know, more than they’ve maybe told us, and we think it’s probably someone that we’ve talked to at some point,” Clarke said. Nearly two decades later, all persons of interest in the case are still alive. “Anyone we feel that’s got direct knowledge, we think is still alive and is still out there.” Clarke strongly encourages anyone who may know something about Eveline’s case to reach out to the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office. “Someone may think of something, like they might not necessarily think it’s important, but it might be the key that lets us start unraveling some of the mysteries behind this.” If you have information regarding Eveline’s death, contact the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office at 740-833-2810 or submit an anonymous tip online. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Woman loses 70 kg to donate kidney to husband, then gives it to a stranger in a paired exchange that saves two lives
articles.summary: Trending News: Five years ago, Rinat Kara was eight months pregnant with twins when she learned that her husband, Meir, urgently needed a kidney donor. She did not h.
articles.body: Five years ago, Rinat Kara was eight months pregnant with twins when she learned that her husband, Meir, urgently needed a kidney donor. She did not hesitate. If someone had to help him, she believed she should be the first to try.There was, however, a major obstacle. Rinat weighed around 130 kilograms after her pregnancy, and doctors told her she needed to lose substantial weight before they could assess her as a donor.The comment from a transplant specialist deeply upset her. But instead of giving up, she turned the challenge into a personal mission. Eighteen months later, she had lost 70 kilograms.“I knew it was on me, that I had to save him,” Rinat told ynetnews.How diabetes damaged Meir’s kidneysMeir, now 41, was diagnosed with diabetes at the age of 12. He admitted that he had not always followed his treatment plan or dietary advice.Over the years, his condition led to serious complications. He lost his sight in both eyes, developed nerve damage in his hands and feet, and eventually experienced kidney failure.His creatinine levels rose sharply, leaving him facing dialysis or a transplant. He eventually spent three months on dialysis while Rinat completed the donor evaluation process.For Meir, dialysis meant spending hours in treatment three times a week. The exhaustion could last for days, leaving little room for ordinary family life.The kidney she prepared to give him went to a strangerTwo weeks before the scheduled operation, a transplant coordinator called Rinat with an unexpected proposal.A 61-year-old patient had spent 16 years on dialysis without finding a suitable donor. Rinat was an exceptionally good match for him.Doctors suggested a paired kidney exchange. Rinat would donate her kidney to the stranger, and Meir would receive a kidney from another willing donor.This arrangement could help two people instead of one.Meir initially worried about what would happen if his transplant failed. Doctors assured him that he would receive priority on the transplant list if that happened. He agreed.Rinat’s surgery went smoothly. Meir’s recovery was harder, with repeated infections and hospitalisations during the first eight months. He later said he was doing well.One donation, two families changedThe kidney Rinat donated helped a man she had never met. Meanwhile, Meir received a kidney from Eitan Nahushtan, a 35-year-old teacher who donated altruistically.The families remain in touch and meet when possible. A decision that began with one woman trying to save her husband eventually connected two donor families and two transplant recipients.For Meir, the greatest relief was leaving dialysis behind. For Rinat, the transplant also marked a personal turning point. She said losing weight had made her more active with her children and helped her feel healthier.“I don't know whether I would have managed it if I hadn't had the goal of saving Meir,” she recalled.The story also carries a lesson about kidney healthRinat and Meir’s experience shows that organ donation does not always follow a simple path. A donor may intend to help one person, yet a paired exchange can make it possible for two patients to receive kidneys.The story also highlights the long-term effects of poorly controlled diabetes. High blood sugar can damage blood vessels and nerves, including those involved in kidney function. Regular treatment, medical follow-up and attention to complications remain important.Rinat says living with one kidney has made little difference to her daily life. However, kidney donors need careful medical evaluation and lifelong follow-up. Donation is a major decision, not a gesture that should be taken lightly.The couple’s story is ultimately about more than sacrifice. It is about how illness can test a family, how strangers can become connected through generosity, and how one difficult decision can change several lives.Disclaimer: This article is based on a report published by ynet news and the personal accounts of Rinat and Meir Kara. It does not establish that every detail of Meir’s earlier treatment was medically inadequate.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: 18-year-old Afghan refugee pleads guilty to murdering man in London; accused of stalking cousin's wife
articles.summary: UK News: An 18-year-old Afghan refugee, Sulaiman Tajzai, has pleaded guilty to the murder of Farmanullah Sherzad in London. The case highlights issues of violence and legal disputes in immigrant communities. Tajzai will be sentenced on September 18. See the full story for more details.
articles.body: An 18-year-old Afghan refugee has pleaded guilty to murdering a 26-year-old man in London after travelling from Leeds with a knife he had bought earlier that day.Sulaiman Tajzai admitted killing Farmanullah Sherzad at the Old Bailey on Friday, the Metropolitan Police said. He also pleaded guilty to possessing a bladed article and is due to be sentenced on September 18, The Independent reported.Tajzai bought the knife near his home in Leeds on March 27 before travelling more than 150 miles to Westminster, where Sherzad lived.Sherzad had been involved in a dispute with Tajzai's cousin and his wife. The couple had previously made complaints to police about him, and he was arrested in October 2025 after officers found him at their Leeds home with his wrists tied.Sherzad told police he was in a relationship with the woman and had travelled to Leeds after she invited him through Snapchat. He was later released, and the couple made further contact with police before being told there would be “no further action” against him.On the night of March 27, Tajzai was waiting near Sherzad's home when Sherzad returned from work at about 10pm. CCTV showed a confrontation outside the property before Tajzai attacked him.Prosecutor Lisa Wilding KC told the court that Sherzad ran “screaming for his life” as Tajzai repeatedly stabbed him.Police were called to Abbey Orchard Street shortly before 10.15pm. Sherzad died at the scene from multiple stab wounds.Tajzai fled and headed towards King's Cross in an attempt to catch a train back to Leeds. He missed his planned service and eventually boarded another train shortly after 6am the next day.He was arrested at his cousin's home in Leeds on March 29. Police searching the property recovered several items belonging to him, including a pair of blood-stained trainers.Investigators also found CCTV evidence showing Tajzai had travelled to London in the weeks before the killing and visited areas around Sherzad's home and workplace.Detective Chief Inspector Wayne Jolley, who led the investigation, described the killing as a “brutal and senseless act of violence”.“No family should have to endure the pain of losing a loved one in such circumstances,” Jolley said.Tajzai will be sentenced at the Old Bailey on September 18.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Cruise passengers erupt over 'rude' luggage habit that sharply divides travelers
articles.summary: Etiquette expert Diane Gottsman of Texas weighed in on the heated cruise elevator debate about travelers using rolling suitcases on packed disembarkation day mornings.
articles.body: Cruise passengers are debating a heated topic among vacation travelers who take to the ocean. Does bringing luggage into crowded ship elevators cross a major etiquette line, especially on hectic disembarkation mornings? Those carrying their own bags often depend on elevators to move between decks as thousands of passengers prepare to leave the ship. Now, social media posts are fueling a broader argument over whether squeezing suitcases into packed elevators is practical or just plain rude. OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT ‘IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT’ AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert based in Texas, said passengers can bring luggage into elevators, though they should be considerate of the limited space. "When it comes to traveling, space is a priority," Gottsman told Fox News Digital. "You always have to think about the people that are going to be around you." Gottsman said passengers can leave larger suitcases outside their cabin the night before for crew members to collect. "When possible, it's always best to keep your suitcases to a minimum when getting on a crowded cruise ship elevator," she said. MAJOR AIRLINE ROASTS PASSENGERS WHO JUMP UP RIGHT AFTER LANDING, IGNITING FIERCE BACKLASH Passengers who prefer to carry their own luggage can do so, she added, but should be prepared to manage it themselves. Cruise lines also have their own procedures for handling bags. Carnival Cruise Line states on its website that checked baggage service during embarkation ends two hours before a ship's scheduled sailing time. "Guests arriving after this time will be responsible for taking their bags on board," the cruise line states. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Planning ahead is especially important on busy embarkation and disembarkation days, Gottsman said. "We know when we're getting off a cruise ship, it's going to be busy," she said. "Everyone is getting off the same cruise ship. So you have to plan in advance." She advised passengers to let others exit before boarding and wait for another elevator if one is already packed. "Don't just charge on with your luggage," Gottsman said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Passengers with mobility issues should also be given priority, while those with extra luggage should be prepared to wait, she added. The issue recently surfaced on Reddit after a first-time cruiser said the traveler and partner were scoffed at by another passenger while taking an elevator from Deck 14 to Deck 5 with their rolling suitcases. Many cruisers defended the couple — arguing that elevators are often the most practical option for passengers carrying luggage across multiple decks. "I always hand-roll my luggage off. I always use the elevator," one Reddit user wrote. "I'm not hauling my bags up and down stairs." Another commenter asked, "How else would you get your luggage down that many decks?" Said another person, "People find any reason to complain [about] a ship elevator. My mom was on a scooter [due to] her bad back/knees, and people were so rude to her at the elevators." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Yet another person chimed in, "The rudeness always seems higher on disembarkation day. You didn’t do anything wrong. I would only use the stairs if it was a flight or two just to save time, otherwise I would definitely use it." "Be cognizant of others and make space when you can," one commenter wrote. Other cruisers said bringing luggage into an elevator is fine as long as passengers remain considerate of those around them. "You can absolutely use the elevators, just be cognizant of others and make space when you can," one commenter wrote. Some disagreed, arguing that using the ship's luggage service can make departure easier for everyone. "The whole point of the luggage delivery is to make it easier for everyone," one person wrote. Cruise industry experts projected a worldwide increase in the number of people taking to the ocean this year — breaking last year’s record, The Associated Press reported several months ago. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In an April report released by the Cruise Lines International Association, an estimated 38.3 million people were projected to travel on ships this year — a number that's 4% higher than last year’s 37.2 million record-breaking number of passengers.

articles.title: Poplar fire: Residents 'did not hear alarms' in fatal tower blaze
articles.summary: Residents say they were alerted by neighbours banging on their doors telling them to leave.
articles.body:
Some residents in an east London tower block have said they did not hear any alarms during a fire in which a man died on the 17th floor.

They told BBC London they had been alerted by neighbours banging on their doors and telling them to leave the building during the early hours of Saturday.

The man died in the flat fire at Neutron Tower in Poplar. Two adults and a child were rescued by firefighters wearing breathing apparatus, the London Fire Brigade (LFB) said.

FirstPort, the building's management company, said "it would not be appropriate for us to speculate on specific matters" while the fire was under investigation.

The LFB said: "There are a range of factors that are being investigated regarding the cause of the fire by the Brigade's Fire Investigation Team."

Residents said they had been alerted to the emergency by neighbours, who went along the corridors banging on doors and telling people to get out of the building.

Katarzyna, who lives on the fifth floor with her husband and two children, said: "A neighbour from the 19th floor, she smelled the smoke from her apartment.

"I heard someone shouting from outside and the neighbours from the 19th floor were outside shouting, 'fire, fire, out'.

"We grabbed our passports and got out - it was pandemonium and my husband was banging on all the doors on the fifth floor to alert neighbours.

"The staircase was pitch black when we walked down, there was no emergency lighting."

She added: "We have smoke and heat alarms in our flats, they did not go off."

Man dies after fire on 17th floor of tower block

Fire on 17th floor of tower block under control

Priya Armstrong-Pond, who lives on the seventh floor, said there had been flooding in the building on Friday.

"Around 5pm, I got a call saying there was water on the stairs and the landing – it was like torrential rain but inside.

"After that there was no water for roughly six hours, but they kept the electric on the whole time. It was on in my flat but not in the communal areas - and all the lifts had water in them as well."

She said she had been alerted by her next-door neighbour at around 04:30 on Saturday.

"He woke up and could hear shouting, so he knocked on everyone's doors," she said. "My neighbour was banging the door, there were no fire alarms going off.

"When we came out there was no lighting at all in the landing and nothing on the stairs. No concierge was there, no one was there to help us.

"By the time we all got downstairs, the whole [17th floor] flat was burnt out and the balcony was all gone."

Armstrong-Pond said many residents were now staying at a nearby hotel, but she had not been told when they would be able to return home.

She said: "People had to book rooms and use their own money."

Katarzyna said she had a hotel room booked until Tuesday, adding: "This building stood like a dark tower last night. It takes you back to Grenfell - a dark building in a sea of light."

FirstPort said it was "deeply saddened" by the man's death and "our thoughts are with his family, and everyone affected by this incident".

"Our immediate priority remains the safety of residents," it said. "All residents have been contacted, and our teams have been providing direct support since the incident, including arranging temporary accommodation where required.

"Our on-site team continues to support those affected and we will keep residents updated as further information becomes available and plans are made for their safe return home."

There was no confirmed timeframe for residents returning to their homes and any decision would be taken in conjunction with the emergency services when it was safe to do so, the firm added.

The LFB said it had been called at 04:35 and the fire was under control by 06:41. Half of the two-bedroom flat and balcony on the 17th floor had been destroyed, it added.

articles.title: Houthis advance in Yemen, attack Saudi Arabia as rebel forces near US base in Djibouti
articles.summary: Middle East News: Fighting intensified in Yemen on Sunday as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea coast, while the Hou.
articles.body: Fighting intensified in Yemen on Sunday as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea coast, while the Houthis claimed attacks on neighbouring Saudi Arabia, escalating fears of a return to a wider civil war.Yemen's internationally recognised government vowed to deploy more forces to the Red Sea after suffering what it described as a “painful” defeat last week, when the Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital shipping route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.The escalation has displaced more than 82,000 people in Yemen since the beginning of September, according to the United Nations migration agency, adding to the humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.Houthis claim attacks on Saudi ArabiaSaudi authorities sounded air-raid sirens on Sunday afternoon in the southern city of Abha and Khamis Mushait province, warning residents to take shelter from possible incoming fire. Both areas have been repeatedly targeted by the Houthis in recent weeks.The Houthis claimed to have launched drones and missiles at targets in Saudi Arabia, including a military base just across the border from Yemen. Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree provided no evidence and did not specify when the alleged attack took place.Saudi civil defence authorities said overnight that a projectile fell in another area near the Yemen border along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. Saudi authorities blamed the Houthis for the attack.Saudi Arabia did not announce any new attacks against Houthi positions.The Houthis have also targeted Saudi oil infrastructure and shipping as part of what they have described as a blockade. Although the group has said it does not intend to threaten commercial shipping from other countries, the attacks have raised concerns in global markets and contributed to renewed pressure on oil prices.Yemen vows to fight backThe National Resistance, a government-allied force that previously controlled parts of the country's western coast, said more than 500 government fighters had been killed along the west coast over the past four weeks. It also said around 1,500 others had been wounded since August 9.The force claimed that more than 1,000 Houthis had been killed in Hodeida and Taiz provinces. A Houthi spokesman did not respond to a request for comment.Sultan al-Arada, a member of Yemen's ruling presidential council, described the collapse of government forces in Mokha and other parts of the western coast as “painful and regrettable”.Al-Arada said in a televised interview aired late Saturday that forces “are currently regrouping and will return to the battle in one form or another.”The Yemeni military said Sunday that it had launched airstrikes on Houthi positions in Mokha, the coastal town of Dhubab and other areas of Taiz province.The Houthis also reported attacks by Saudi-backed forces in the province and artillery shelling in Saada province, their stronghold near Yemen's northern border with Saudi Arabia.Houthi advance nears US base in DjiboutiThe Houthi advance has brought the group to within around 20 miles (32 kilometres) of a major US military base in Djibouti, located across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The base is the main US military installation in Africa and is located alongside facilities operated by China, France and Japan.Djibouti is also facing a growing humanitarian challenge as Yemenis flee across the dangerous waters separating the two countries.More than 2,000 Yemenis have reached Djibouti, according to the International Organization for Migration.Djibouti's Economy and Finance Minister Ilyas M. Dawaleh said on X that the country's navy, coast guard and other specialised agencies were carrying out rescue operations and providing emergency assistance.Displaced Yemenis fear another warThe latest escalation has deepened fears among Yemenis that the country could once again descend into a prolonged civil war.Yemen has more than 40 million people and has already endured a conflict that killed around 150,000 people and pushed millions towards famine.The internationally recognised Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia have been fighting the Houthis for 12 years, although a ceasefire that began in 2022 had largely halted major fighting.People fleeing the latest Houthi advance told The Associated Press that government forces had withdrawn from some areas and urged residents to flee.At a camp in Aden, Ahmad al-Masawi, director of the Al Salam camp, described the condition of displaced people as desperate.“The displaced people are in a very bad condition,” said Ahmad al-Masawi, the director of the Al Salam camp in the southern port city of Aden, who appealed to international organizations for assistance. “They left their homes quickly without any clothing or anything. They are crammed in camps, houses and even on roads."Hussein Haydara sat outside a shelter at the camp as his children waited to be assigned a tent. He said he was worried about the distance from schools, hospitals and markets and questioned how his family would survive in the coming weeks and months.Haydara had previously fled his home in Hodaida after the Houthis seized it in 2015. He said the latest displacement had been even more difficult because families had little time to prepare.“With the first displacement, we had time to plan things but this time we were forced to escape all of a sudden. One could hardly take their children and the lightest stuff possible,” he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
